title: Reference A's baseline: the bottom line for dm's speed, memory and CPU
never: This file never changes. bench/compare.mjs and the xtask test `the_reference_a_baseline_never_changes` hold it to its SHA-256. A new measurement of reference A goes into a new file beside it, never into this one.
rule: dm passes a scenario when every run's file is whole and, for every metric with a direction, dm's median over its runs is lower than reference A's floor (equal passes only where the floor is 0).

A floor is the best value reference A reached in any whole run of that scenario and group: the strictest bar it has set, so a run of reference A slowed by the harness can only have made a floor easier, never harder.

Metrics marked time, in the machine-bound scenarios (fast, big40), are scaled to the computer dm runs on by the ceiling: floor x min(1, ceiling there / ceiling here), each the best of its runs. A floor never gets looser than it is here.
Every other floor applies as it is, on every system: the capped scenarios are bound by the server's caps and not the computer, and memory and CPU are bars to come in under.
The default group is standard. A run with BENCH_DM_CONNECTIONS=16 is judged against connections16.

machine.note: Both apps on the same computer, run one after the other, never at once; each repetition alternated which went first, 3 s apart.

referenceA.settings: its own defaults: 8 connections, its temporary folder on C:, nothing else changed; for connections16 its connection number set to 16 in its Options
referenceA.given: by its own command line, silently (/d <address> /p <folder> /n), as a browser hands it a download; for batch each file queued (/a) then the queue started (/s)
referenceA.windows: its question boxes and download-finished boxes answered by the window helper (bench/refa-windows.ps1), never with a blocking call; in its final form only until the server saw the first request (so it takes no CPU from the download) and once after the file was whole
referenceA.done: the file at its full size in its folder, looked at every 100 ms, then its SHA-256 compared

dmThen.version: 0.9.0 and the builds of 2026-11-10 after it (gaps rows 166 to 168), the egui window
dmThen.given: through its control port (downloads.add), its window shown, a home of its own (BENCH_DM_HOME), settings.json giving only the download folder (and connections for connections16)
dmThen.done: its row says completed (queue.list every 100 ms), then the SHA-256 of the file it names compared

groups.standard: 8 connections (both apps' default); dm's home on C:, both apps saving to the hard disk D:; reference A's temporary parts on C: (its default)
groups.connections16: as standard, with both apps set to 16 connections
groups.allSsd: as standard, with everything on C: (the SSD)
groups.allSsdConnections16: as allSsd, with both apps set to 16 connections

server.where: Node http server on 127.0.0.1, in the harness process, one path prefix and one log per run
server.headers: Content-Type application/octet-stream, Accept-Ranges bytes, ETag "<first 12 hex of the SHA-256>", Last-Modified Mon, 01 Jan 2024 00:00:00 GMT, Content-Length
server.ranges: bytes=a-b, bytes=a- and bytes=-n answered 206 with Content-Range; a start past the end 416
server.writes: pieces of 1 MiB with no cap, 64 KiB under a cap; never less than 16 KiB (or what is left); a capped write waits 4 ms and tries again
server.perConnectionCap: token bucket per connection, at most 128 KiB banked
server.totalCap: token bucket shared by all connections of the run, at most 256 KiB banked
server.cuts: flaky: each connection closed after a uniform random 0.25 to 3 MiB (xorshift32 seeded 0xC0FFEE per run)
server.outage: outage: once 30% of the file is served, every connection is closed and every request in the next 15 s is closed as it arrives

harness.data: a 1 MiB xorshift32 block seeded with 1000 + 7 x file index + the length of the scenario name, repeated, each 4 KiB stamped with (MiB index XOR 0x9e3779b9), so a piece put in the wrong place changes the SHA-256
harness.sampler: every 400 ms: working set, private bytes and CPU time of each app process (Windows: Get-Process; Linux: /proc; macOS: ps); a peak is the highest sample from the address handed over to 400 ms after done; CPU the time at the last sample less the time at the last sample before the start

idle.label: window up, nothing to do, 20 s

per_conn.label: 64 MiB, each connection 1 MiB/s
per_conn.ideal: 64 MiB over 8 connections of 1 MiB/s (more connections can do better)

flaky.label: 64 MiB at 8 MiB/s, every connection cut after 0.25-3 MiB

outage.label: 64 MiB at 8 MiB/s, all connections fail for 15 s at 30%
outage.ideal: 64 MiB at 8 MiB/s plus the 15 s outage

batch.label: 24 files of 2 MiB, each connection 2 MiB/s, all added at once
batch.ideal: 48 MiB at 2 MiB/s a connection: 3 s with 8 connections at once, less with more

big40.label: 512 MiB at 40 MiB/s in all
big40.bound: machine on the baseline computer (Windows' timer, about 15.6 ms, holds the harness's paced server near 19 MiB/s, below its 40 MiB/s cap); the cap elsewhere

metrics.what: from the moment the address is handed to the app to the file whole on disk
from the first request at the server to the file whole on disk (the engine alone)
from the address handed over to the first request at the server
from the last byte sent to the file whole on disk (the finish: assembling, moving, checking)
bytes served beyond the file size, as a share of it (fetched twice)
peak working set (resident memory) while downloading, sampled every 400 ms
peak private bytes (anonymous memory on Linux; not sampled on macOS)
CPU time used from the address handed over to the file whole
from the outage ending to the next byte served (outage only)
most files being sent at once (batch)
requests dropped during the outage (how hard the app retried)

ceiling.client: bench/ceiling-client.mjs (8 ranges at once, each into a file of its own through a 4 MiB buffered stream)
ceiling.writtenTo: the hard disk D:, the download folder of the standard group

batch.why: reference A finished no run with every file whole (see the runs)

notMeasured.batch: Reference A finished 3 and 4 of the 24 files within the 300 s allowed when its queue was filled and started from its command line; that says more about how the harness starts its queue than about reference A (gaps row 172). No floor: dm's batch is judged against its ideal until a run of reference A given the files as a person gives them is frozen in a file of its own.
notMeasured.inet: Public files over the internet: never a floor, the network is not the same twice.
